changes.headline: OPEC+ rolls November targets; crude fades on the overnight tape
changes.dek: November targets held; WTI ~$89.69 overnight (-1.6%); Brent ~$101.67 (-0.9%). OPEC+ held November production targets steady on Sunday: the seven core members (Saudi Arabia, Russia, Iraq, Kuwait, Algeria, Kazakhstan, Oman) in a brief virtual meeting, no quota changes, next meeting November 1. The seven pumped 25.0 Mb/d in August (+630 kb/d m/m), still ~5 Mb/d below pre-war February, with ~2 Mb/d of cuts through year-end and the 2027 capacity review delayed. UBS's Giovanni Staunovo: market 'remains tight.' The Sunday-night tape faded anyway: WTI ~$89.69 (-1.6% vs Friday's $91.11 settle), Brent ~$101.67 (-0.9% vs Friday's Dec $102.25). The marginal seller is the G7 release calendar and intact flows, not OPEC+.
changes.balance_read: Flat price trades escalation optionality, not missing barrels (Middle East shipments ~98% of pre-war, 40% of September Gulf volumes bypassing Hormuz via pipeline): the roll removed the left tail rather than adding anything.
changes.publishers: Reuters, Oct 4, 2026; Yahoo front-month futures session print ~02:00 MDT

changes.headline: Products re-tighten overnight as the release details get smaller
changes.dek: ING gasoil $85->$70; diesel export ban ruled out; 50/50 split unconfirmed. ING marked the ICE gasoil crack from ~$85/bbl mid-last week to ~$70 this morning, adding the only permanent fix for distillate tightness is refined products flowing from the Persian Gulf again. Weekend reporting on the G7 release: no country-by-country volume breakdown published; the 50/50 diesel/crude split from Friday's first reporting is NOT confirmed by any weekend source. What stands: 'substantial' diesel front-loaded in the first 20 days, IEA follow-up within 20 days. Confirmed: the US president ruled out a diesel export ban (Saturday); Canada, the only G7 nation without a strategic reserve, will coordinate refinery maintenance schedules. NYMEX diesel crack closed $97.94 Friday (first sub-$100 after eighteen straight above); the Sunday-night session print has it back at ~$102 (provisional, not a close).
changes.balance_read: The release is the ceiling on the product market; the physical drivers (Russia's diesel export ban through Oct 31, China's October product-export halt) are the floor. The first 20 days of front-loaded diesel run straight into the Russian ban's Oct 31 expiry.
changes.publishers: ING Commodities Feed, Oct 5; G7 statement via OGE Journal, Oct 3; validated crack history refreshed Oct 5

changes.headline: WCS front holds its widening into the roll
changes.dek: TMW Nov26 -$24.13; Dec26 -$24.65 (widest); ARV-TMW +$9.28. TMW (ICE WCS 1A) EOD Oct 2: Nov26 -$24.13 (-$0.38), Dec26 -$24.65 (-$0.40, widest tenor on the strip), Jan27 -$23.30 down the strip to Oct27 -$17.20. The front three widened ~$0.38-0.40 on Friday while flat price recovered into the close. Cross-grades: ARV Nov26 -$14.86 (-$0.31), ARV-TMW arb +$9.28: the constraint sits at the egress end. TMU +$3.40; TMF +$3.85 holding into diluent season; TMS +$5.98, SYN-WCS $30.11. WCS Nov outright ~$66.98.
changes.balance_read: A diesel release does not add a single barrel of egress at Kerrobert. The diff trades the November-December egress crunch; flat price trades the war. They are different markets.
changes.publishers: ICE Report Center end-of-day settlements, Oct 2, 2026 (all six contracts)

changes.headline: Hormuz: four strikes in 72 hours, flows intact
changes.dek: Sunday: Lipsi struck (engine-room damage); JMIC: 4 attacks in 72h; no new strike Oct 5. The Liberia-flagged Aframax Lipsi (newbuild, delivered Aug 2026) was struck by an unknown projectile transiting Hormuz on Sunday: engine-room damage, crew safe, no environmental impact. JMIC counts up to four attacks in the strait in the 72 hours Oct 2-4. No new strike reported Oct 5. Flows: Middle East shipments ~17.5 Mb/d (~98% of pre-war, JPMorgan); Hormuz itself ~12.8 Mb/d in September; ~40% of September Gulf volumes bypassed the strait via Saudi/UAE pipelines. Ceasefire: no new movement; Iran reviewing the US counterproposal received via Qatar. Escalation: no new movement; three US carriers in region by end-October, full buildup (3 carriers + 2 amphibious groups, 20,000+ personnel) by end-November.
changes.balance_read: Ships struck near-daily, barrels flowing at 98%. The market prices the trajectory (escalation risk vs. the ceasefire track), not the body count.
changes.publishers: UKMTO via Riviera Maritime Media; JPMorgan; Kpler via OilPrice, Oct 3-4, 2026

changes.headline: Demand returns (Joliet) while supply healing stays unconfirmed (Syncrude)
changes.dek: Joliet back (~275 kb/d); Syncrude completion unconfirmed; Pacific Link designated; EIA: Cushing 24.3M, gasoline lowest since 2014. Joliet confirmed back in service (QCIntel Sep 28; PriceGroup Sep 29): ~275 kb/d of PADD 2 heavy-crude demand returning; the diff-direction rule runs wider-while-offline, snap-tighter-on-restart. Syncrude Mildred Lake turnaround: no public confirmation of completion; guided window runs into mid-October per the trades schedule. BP Whiting: lockout of ~800 USW workers continues since March; the 'union walked' claim comes from the company's Sep 29 statement alone, no independent confirmation, no strike vote. October Mainline apportionment 8% lights / 4% heavies at Kerrobert (Enbridge, Sep 16); November notice ~mid-October. Pacific Link (~1 Mb/d, Edmonton to Roberts Bank) designated Oct 1 as a project of national interest; Ottawa/Alberta additionally seeking 300-400 kb/d within the existing TMX system; China ~60% of TMX seaborne exports. DRA: in service January 2027 (standing authority); weekend OilPrice 'by year-end' language reads as approval timing, not in-service. EIA w/e Sep 25: crude +0.922M to 427.3M; Cushing +0.553M to 24.3M (highest since May); gasoline -1.684M to 204.4M (lowest since Nov 2014); distillates -2.251M to 105.2M (14% below 5-yr avg); refinery util 92.5%; US prod 14.0 Mb/d. Canada oil rigs 147 (+4, second up week).
changes.balance_read: The tightening leg for Oct/Nov WCS is demand returning (Joliet); the softening leg is SCO supply normalizing (Syncrude, unconfirmed) plus Q4 refinery demand stepping off. Long-dated projects change the 2028+ math; the November crunch trades on the apportionment notice.
changes.publishers: QCIntel/PriceGroup Sep 28-29; Enbridge notice Sep 16; EIA WPSR Sep 30; Baker Hughes Oct 2

forward_calendar.detail: Delivery November-December; replacement interest 7.5%/9.5% far cheaper than June's 18%, this round expected to place. Sparta watching Dec Mars FOB below $1/bbl. Award after Oct 6 is the next real data point for Gulf sour pricing.
